subject: general
question: Which of the following is the largest source of electricity generation in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermal power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thermal power is the **largest source of electricity generation in India**, contributing significantly to the country’s overall energy production.
 
• As of recent statistics, thermal power accounts for approximately **60-70% of India’s total electricity generation**.
 
• Thermal power plants in India primarily use **coal, gas, and oil** as fuel sources, with coal being the most dominant.
 
• India is the second-largest consumer of coal globally, and coal-fired thermal power plants are widespread across the nation.
 
• Major thermal power plants include the **Vindhyachal Thermal Power Station** (Madhya Pradesh) and **Mundra Thermal Power Station** (Gujarat).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solar energy**

 
 
• Solar energy contributes to a smaller share of India’s electricity generation compared to thermal power but is growing rapidly.
 
• India has ambitious renewable energy targets and aims to achieve **280 GW of solar power capacity by 2030** under its National Solar Mission.
 
• Prominent solar plants include the **Bhadla Solar Park** (Rajasthan) and **Pavagada Solar Park** (Karnataka).
 
 
 
• **Nuclear energy**
 
 
• Nuclear energy contributes about **2-3% of India’s total electricity generation**.
 
• India has operational nuclear reactors in states like Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, and Rajasthan, with the **Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant** being one of the largest.
 
• Nuclear power is considered a clean energy source and is part of India’s long-term energy diversification strategy.
 
 
 
• **Wind energy**
 
 
• Wind energy is a significant renewable energy source in India, especially in states like Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.
 
• It contributes around **10% of India’s total electricity generation** and is the largest renewable energy source in the country.
 
• India has a target of achieving **140 GW of wind power capacity by 2030**.
